NARRATIVE AND PLANS FOR TYPE 1 ZONING AMENDMENT FOR
4525-31 NORTH CLARK STREET, CHICAGO IL

The subject property is located within a Transit-Served Location (“TSL”), as it is situated along
the Clark Street Bus Corridor and within the applicable distance of the CTA Red Line Wilson
Station. The subject property is currently improved with an existing commercial building that is
partially vacant. The Applicant proposes to demolish the existing improvement and redevelop the
property with a new four-story mixed-use building containing commercial space on the first floor,
nine dwelling units on the upper floors, and a private garage containing ten accessory off-street
parking spaces. In order to permit the proposed development, the Applicant seeks a zoning map
amendment to establish a C1-3 Neighborhood Commercial District, together with optional relief
by variation and administrative adjustment, as applicable, from certain applicable bulk standards.
Specifically, the requested relief includes: (i) a reduction of the required rear setback from 30 feet
to 20 feet; (ii) a reduction of the required transparent window area from 244.8 square feet to 198
square feet; and (iii) an increase in the number of accessory off-street parking spaces from four
spaces required to ten spaces proposed.

I. The applicant will comply with Section 17-4-0301 Specific Criteria for Transit-Served
Locations, should such provisions be determined as applicable:

17-4-0301 Specific Criteria for Transit-Served Locations. In D districts, any new construction
within 2,640 feet of a CTA or METRA rail station entrance or exit must satisfy all of the
following specific criteria:

J. The project complies with the applicable standards of Section 17-10-0102-B Transit-Served
Locations:

The subject property is a Transit Served Location, as it is situated along the Clark Street Bus
Corridor and within the applicable distance of the CTA Red Line Wilson Station.

2. The project complies with the standards and regulations of Section 17-4-0504, except paragraph H
if the project is not located along a pedestrian street and except paragraph C if the land use is
designated in a non-commercial use group, pertaining to pedestrian streets and pedestrian retail
streets, even if the project is not located along a pedestrian street or a pedestrian retail street;

(a) The entire building fagade abuts the sidewalk or is located within 5 feet of the sidewalk.

(b) The proposed redevelopment substantially complies with the requirements of Section 17-4-
0504-C Transparency standards: the commercial space will provide clear, non-reflective windows;
subject to the variation relief as described below.

(c) The building will have a primary entrance door facing Clark Street.

(d) All off-street parking spaces will be located within enclosed garage and will not be visible
from the right-of-way.

(e) The parking area will be located inside the garage; vehicle access to the parking area will come
via the public alley, per site plan attached.

3. The project complies with the general goals set forth in the Transit Friendly Development Guide:
Station Area Typology, and any other station-specific plans, designs or guidelines adopted by the
Chicago Plan Commission.

This Criteria is not applicable to this project.

4. Residential building projects shall not have a number of parking spaces in excess of 50% of the
Minimum Automobile Parking Ratio for the applicable district listed in Section 17-10-0208 with
any fractional result rounded up to the next higher whole number, unless additional parking spaces
are approved as an administrative adjustment under the provisions of Section 17-13-1003-EE; and

With this proposed redevelopment, the Applicant is proposing a parking ratio which is in excess
of 50% of the Minimum Automobile Parking Ratio for the applicable district listed in Section 17-
10-0208 — see the request for an administrative adjustment below.

5. The project complies with the Travel Demand Study and Management Plan rules of the Chicago
Department of Transportation. The City's Commissioner of Transportation is authorized to issue
Travel Demand Study and Management Plan rules consistent with this section.

This Criteria is not applicable to this project.

Il. Optional Relief for Adjustment and Variation under Section 17-13-0303-D —

a Type 1 map amendment pursuant to Section 17-13-0300, may include relief available
pursuant to Section 17-13-1000 or 17-13-1100; in such instances, City Council approval of a
Type-1 application containing said elements shall preclude subsequent review otherwise
required pursuant to Sections 17-13-1000 or 17-13-1100, provided that no Type 1
application permits issued may be in violation of Section 17-13-0310:

(A) _ The Applicant seeks relief for variation under section 17-13-1101-B, from the rear setback
requirements of Section 17-3-0405-A, which states that for floors containing dwelling
units, the minimum rear setback is 30 feet. To mitigate site planning hardships on this
substandard lot, the Applicant requests a reduction in the required rear setback from 30
feet required to 20 feet proposed to account for the pillars supporting rear balconies.

(B) _ The Applicant seeks relief for administrative adjustment under Section 17-13-1003-Q
Pedestrian Streets — Transparent Window Standards, which provides for adjustment to the ©
transparent window area standards of Sec. 17-3-0504-C, to allow up to a 25% reduction in
the amount of transparent window area required. Since the front ground floor elevations
must incorporate both commercial and residential entry, the project needs small reduction
in the transparency standards from 244.8 SF required to 198 SF proposed.

(C) The Applicant seeks relief for administrative adjustment under Section under the
provisions of Section 17-13-1003-EE from the parking regulations of Section 17-4-0301
Specific Criteria for Transit-Served Locations, to increase the parking ratio, from 5 spaces

required to 10 spaces proposed.

(@) =‘ The Applicant is seeking all relief necessary, as allowed by the Zoning Ordinance, for
the proposed development per the attached Type 1 Plans.

In support of this request, the Applicant states the following:

1. Strict compliance with the regulations and standards of this Zoning Ordinance would
create practical difficulties and hardships for the subject property, since the subject
property has a substandard depth.

2. The requested variations are consistent with the stated purpose and intent of this Zoning

Ordinance since this proposed redevelopment and corresponding variations are compatible
with the existing land use pattern on the subject block, where majority of the zoning lots
are already improved with multi-story and multi-unit mixed-use and residential buildings.
Furthermore, the new dwelling units will increase the variety of available housing stock,
in response to the growing housing demand in the neighborhood.
